macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats and investors weigh Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices steadied and markets reassessed the impact of renewed U.S.-Iran conflict on risk assets. Reuters said European shares also rose in choppy trading, while investors monitored whether geopolitical stress would prolong inflation pressure and keep bonds under strain.

items.title: Oil prices, dollar and bonds remain under pressure from renewed Middle East conflict
items.summary: Reuters reported that oil rose on fresh U.S. strikes against Iran, reviving inflation fears and supporting the U.S. dollar, while the 10-year Japanese government bond yield hit a 30-year high as investors worried about inflation and fiscal health. The same Reuters roundup said Asian shares gained only modestly because surging oil capped risk appetite.

items.title: Fed caution and higher oil prices weigh on Asian-Pacific markets
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian shares wobbled as Fed caution tempered optimism from lower oil prices, while Japan’s Topix rose and the Nikkei lagged on tech weakness. The same feed highlighted yen weakness near multi-decade lows, underscoring continued pressure on global financial conditions.

items.title: OPEC+ agrees modest output increase as oil slides
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that seven OPEC+ countries agreed to lift combined oil output targets by 188,000 barrels per day in August, adding supply as crude prices fell back from recent highs. The move was described as a response to the market’s recent oil spike tied to the Iran conflict.

items.title: PepsiCo beats revenue estimates despite softer North American demand
items.summary: Yahoo Finance and CNBC reported that PepsiCo posted stronger-than-expected second-quarter revenue of $24.2 billion, even as it cited weaker demand in North America and pressure from cautious consumers. CNBC also noted the stock was among the biggest premarket movers after the release.

items.title: US benchmark equity indexes lower amid oil-driven risk-off move
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that U.S. benchmark equity indexes were lower intraday as investors reacted to the ceasefire breakdown and a sharp jump in oil prices. Treasury yields also steadied after the previous session’s spike, reflecting caution around inflation and growth.

items.title: Inflation and central bank tightening stay in focus globally
items.summary: The Financial Times said New Zealand raised rates for the first time in three years, while IMF coverage highlighted rising inflation risks and Reuters noted some Fed officials still saw the need for future rate increases to contain price pressures. Reuters also cited India inflation likely moving above the central bank’s 4% target and China’s producer inflation staying elevated.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market rebounds as Iran-U.S. tensions ease; Bitcoin holds above $65K
items.summary: Bitcoin rose to about $65,229, while Ethereum traded near $1,944 and the total crypto market cap climbed to about $2.23 trillion as risk sentiment improved after reports that the U.S. and Iran had paused mutual strikes. CoinDesk also reported Bitcoin around $65,318 and Ether near $1,963, with Ether outperforming Bitcoin on the day.

items.title: BitMart shuts down after nine years; BMX token plunges sharply
items.summary: CryptoRank reported that centralized exchange BitMart shut down after nine years, triggering a roughly 58% crash in its BMX token. The move highlighted ongoing exchange-risk concerns even as the broader market rebounded.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether gain on risk-on move tied to Middle East de-escalation
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin rose after the U.S. and Iran held off further strikes, with investors viewing the pause as supportive for risk assets. The rally followed weakness in oil and a broader lift in stock futures.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly spikes above $65,600 in futures trading before easing
items.summary: CoinDesk said Bitcoin briefly spiked to about $65,600 at the start of futures trading before settling near $65,200, while the CoinDesk 20 Index rose modestly over 24 hours. Ether also edged higher and approached the $2,000 level for the first time since early June.

items.title: Regulatory focus intensifies as U.S. crypto bill fight moves toward key vote
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that the CLARITY Act is facing a key Senate test, while The Block noted Senator Wyden urged leaders to preserve blockchain developer protections in the broader crypto bill. The developments signal that U.S. crypto policy remains a major market driver.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules amid market expansion
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong's SFC is forcing crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, reflecting a continued push for stronger operational security. The report adds to a broader wave of Asia-Pacific crypto regulation updates.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based payment system with 17 banks in pilot
items.summary: Newsbit reported that Swift launched a blockchain network for cross-border payments outside normal business hours, with 17 banks participating in pilot tests. The move is a notable traditional-finance adoption signal for blockchain infrastructure.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation cuts budget and headcount as it shifts treasury strategy
items.summary: Coin Insider reported that the Ethereum Foundation will cut its budget by 40% and headcount by 20%, moving toward an endowment model with a target of 5% annual treasury spending after 2030. The change signals a significant governance and resource-management shift for the Ethereum ecosystem.

items.title: BlackRock deposits large BTC and ETH amounts to Coinbase
items.summary: Odaily reported that BlackRock transferred substantial Bitcoin and Ethereum holdings to Coinbase, citing on-chain monitoring data. The flows were widely watched because of BlackRock's outsized influence in institutional crypto markets.

items.title: Binance advances new leveraged OUSDT perpetual contract listing
items.summary: Odaily reported that Binance will list the OUSDT perpetual contract with up to 10x leverage. The listing reflects continued demand for derivatives activity despite mixed spot-market sentiment.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI unveils ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agent in ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The release is part of OpenAI’s broader push into enterprise automation.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded 1.1 version, extending its strategy to monetize AI models directly. The move puts Meta in sharper competition with Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The capability is especially relevant for live translation and more natural voice agents.

items.title: SpaceXAI releases Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agentic workflows. The release adds to the rapid pace of new frontier-model launches.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing its own AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September as it expands computing capacity. The company is also working toward a much larger internal compute target next year.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta said it will build a massive data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to support growing AI infrastructure needs. The project reflects the industry’s continuing emphasis on compute expansion.

items.title: Micron plans more than $250 billion in U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging demand for memory chips in the AI era. The announcement underscores how AI is reshaping semiconductor capital spending.

items.title: Chinese AI firms push for tighter domestic tech stack
items.summary: Reuters reported that China is seeking to build a more self-contained AI ecosystem, including open-source models, as Washington tightens access to advanced AI technology. The trend points to growing geopolitical fragmentation in AI development.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox restructuring triggers studio closures and layoffs
items.summary: Multiple reports say Microsoft’s latest gaming reset is leading to major cuts, including studio closures, divestments, and layoffs across Xbox-linked teams. Coverage also says some projects have lost funding as Microsoft shifts its portfolio strategy.

items.title: Capcom moves up 'Onimusha: Way of the Sword' release date
items.summary: Capcom has reportedly brought forward the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword, moving it from September 25 to September 4. The change makes it one of the most notable release-date updates in the last day.

items.title: Nintendo confirms 'Mario Kart Tour' shutdown after 7 years
items.summary: Nintendo has announced that Mario Kart Tour will be shut down this September, with no offline version planned. That makes it one of the biggest mobile-game service-ending stories in the latest news cycle.

items.title: Square Enix announces 'Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis' removal from app stores
items.summary: Square Enix said Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis will be removed from app stores on October 7, 2026, as the game approaches the end of its distribution lifecycle. The announcement is one of the clearest industry-service developments in the past 24 hours.

items.title: Moonshot Games ends continued development on 'Wildgate'
items.summary: Moonshot Games has announced it is stopping continued development of Wildgate after failing to build a durable player base. The decision reflects ongoing pressure on live-service multiplayer games to maintain traction.

items.title: 'Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced' launches on Steam and posts strong player numbers
items.summary: The fan-made Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced has launched on Steam and is already drawing unusually high concurrent-player counts. Reports say it has outperformed prior series peaks on the platform.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports arrive on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: New ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 are now available on PS4 and PS5. Coverage notes that the releases come at a premium price.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks 10th anniversary with livestream announcements
items.summary: Pokémon Go’s 10th-anniversary celebration featured a livestream with live announcements and surprises. The event stands out as one of the day’s key mobile and live-service game updates.

items.title: Rockstar teases next GTA Online update, 'The Kortz Center Heist'
items.summary: Rockstar has confirmed the next major GTA Online update, The Kortz Center Heist, is set for release next week. Fans have already spotted Easter eggs tied to Rockstar properties in the lead-up.

items.title: US gaming spending falls sharply in June amid hardware comparison effects
items.summary: Video game spending in the U.S. fell 21% in June, according to commentary highlighted in gaming coverage. The decline was tied in part to comparison effects around last year’s Switch 2 launch and other market factors.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Swift introduced a blockchain-based shared ledger to support round-the-clock payments and compete with stablecoin networks. Citi and HSBC are among the initial participating banks.

items.title: India removes import duty on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped duties on selected mobile phone and electronics components, cutting levies of 7.5% and 5%. The move could lower costs for manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion in Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple plans to invest over $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom. The deal also includes Broadcom expanding a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans in-house AI chip manufacturing from September
items.summary: According to an internal memo, Meta plans to begin manufacturing its own AI chip in September. The move is part of a broader effort to increase computing capacity.

items.title: EU lawmakers back temporary rules on child sexual abuse detection
items.summary: EU lawmakers supported a proposal to restore temporary rules allowing platforms such as Google and Meta to detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The measure affects major online services and moderation policy.

items.title: MFE-MediaForEurope plans single streaming platform across Europe
items.summary: MFE-MediaForEurope said it plans to combine technologies from its Italian and German businesses into one streaming platform. The broadcaster is trying to compete more directly with global digital and advertising rivals.

items.title: IBM launches new z17 mainframe and LinuxOne server models
items.summary: IBM unveiled new models in its z17 mainframe series and LinuxOne server line. The updates are aimed at helping customers fit more computing power into constrained data-center space.

items.title: Meta announces in-house smart glasses designed for lower cost
items.summary: Meta introduced a new line of smart glasses designed internally, signaling a deeper push into wearable devices. The company is positioning the product as a cheaper alternative in the category.
